findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Sharpen sketch #2: state that the discriminating signal is a helper reading env through a NON-LITERAL (parameter) name argument, not merely 'contains an env read', and acknowledge that even that must exclude terminal direct-readers (e.g. _snapshot_int, review_bot/opcert config readers that also take an env_name param) so it does not collide with AC3's no-false-positives constraint.

Direct env readers NOT in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS exist throughout the tree: src/rebar/config.py:121/360/502, src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:75/89/230/305, src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:90/104/228/238, src/rebar/opcert_service/config.py:72/102 — all would be flagged by the literal wording

The true distinguishing signal is a NON-LITERAL name argument: _llm_float/_llm_int/_llm_str do os.environ.get(env_name) with env_name a parameter (src/rebar/llm/config.py:376/391/411); but _snapshot_int (src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:305), review_bot/config.py:228/238 and opcert_service/config.py:72 also take an env_name parameter yet are terminal readers whose literal is registered at the call site, so 'takes an env_name param' alone still over-matches

findings.location: Problem section, 'Why it is harder than the os.environ half' bullet 2 and the following 'Note the second option would have caught b00f exactly.'
